name: Dolphin
funFacts: Dolphins are actually mammals that breathe air, not fish!
They can swim up to 20 miles per hour!
Dolphins sleep with one eye open and half their brain awake!
Each dolphin has a unique whistle, like a name!
Dolphins use echolocation to 'see' with sound!

ageContent.3-5: Dolphins are friendly animals that live in the ocean! They love to jump and play in the waves. Dolphins talk to each other with clicks and whistles. They're not fish - they breathe air just like you!
ageContent.6-8: Dolphins are super smart marine mammals! Unlike fish, they breathe air through a blowhole on top of their head. Dolphins are very social and live in groups called pods. They have their own special whistle that's like their name - other dolphins recognize them by it! Dolphins use echolocation to find food - they make clicking sounds and listen for the echo to know where things are. They can even see with sound!
ageContent.9-12: Dolphins are highly intelligent marine mammals known for their social behavior, playfulness, and cognitive abilities. They belong to the cetacean family, which includes whales. Dolphins use echolocation - emitting clicks and interpreting the returning echoes - to navigate and hunt in murky water. Their brains are remarkably large relative to body size, and they demonstrate self-awareness, problem-solving, and teaching behaviors. Dolphins sleep by resting one half of their brain at a time, allowing them to continue swimming and breathing. There are around 40 species of dolphins, ranging from the 4-foot Maui's dolphin to the 30-foot orca (yes, orcas are dolphins!).
